jp: 弟[おとうと]は部屋[へや]を片付[かたづ]けないので、このままだと大事[だいじ]な書類[しょるい]もなくし{かねない|pt-kanenai}。
en: My brother never tidies his room, so at this rate he could well lose important documents too.
why: Stem + かねない warns that something bad may well happen.

jp: 我[わ]が家[や]のルールは私[わたし]一人[ひとり]では決[き]め{かねる|pt-kanenai}ので、家族[かぞく]で相談[そうだん]します。
en: I can't decide our household rules on my own, so I'll talk it over with my family.
why: Stem + かねる means being unable to do something (here, decide alone).

jp: 毎日[まいにち]少[すこ]しずつ続[つづ]ければ、誰[だれ]でも料理[りょうり]が上手[じょうず]になり{得[う]る|pt-kanenai}。
en: If you keep at it a little every day, anyone can become good at cooking.
why: Stem + 得る says something is possible; かねない would suggest a bad outcome.

jp: 母[はは]が作[つく]ってくれる味噌汁[みそしる]の味[あじ]は、何物[なにもの]にも代[か]え{がたい|pt-kanenai}。
en: Nothing can replace the taste of the miso soup my mother makes.
why: Stem + がたい means something is hard to do; 何物にも代えがたい is the set phrase for 'irreplaceable'.

jp: 毎晩[まいばん]連絡[れんらく]もせずに遅[おそ]く帰[かえ]る夫[おっと]の気持[きも]ちは、理解[りかい]し{がたい|pt-kanenai}。
en: I find it hard to understand my husband, who comes home late every night without even calling.
why: Stem + がたい means something is hard to do, here hard to understand; 得る would mean it is understandable.
